# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->

dabestr is the principal R implementation of estimation statistics, a data-analysis framework that reports effect sizes and confidence intervals in place of null-hypothesis significance testing. It is on CRAN and developed openly on GitHub, and implements methods described in two papers from our group (Ho et al. 2019; Lu et al. 2026). It has grown from two-group mean differences into a package spanning repeated measures, delta–delta (2×2) designs, mini-meta analysis, and binary proportions.

That growth has outpaced the original architecture. First-class statistical concepts are encoded implicitly across the arguments of one entry-point function, a set of design flags, and a heterogeneous result object that the plotting layer inspects directly. The package works, but is increasingly hard to extend, test, and integrate with the R ecosystem.

**Proposal.** A focused modernization that makes the existing statistical grammar explicit: a documented, standardized, composable estimation-result object (built on S7), computation separated from visualization, the current implementation frozen as a regression target, and full backward compatibility. No new statistical methodology is proposed; consolidating the engineering keeps scientific risk low and yields infrastructure other R packages can build on.

**Deliverables (6 milestones, 9 months).** (1) architecture specification and result-object schema; (2) frozen regression corpus in CI; (3) standardized result object with tidy accessors; (4) plots refactored onto the public contract; (5) backward-compatibility layer, deprecation path, and simplified delta–delta interface; (6) documentation, contributor guide, and CRAN release. Budget: USD $10,000, all developer labor, allocated by milestone and paid on the ISC’s standard 50%/50% schedule.
